task.description: Diagnosis complete (reproduced directly from source, not from the issue report's prose). Design a fix for lib/letflow/dlq/entry.ex's insert_changeset/2 per the scope below.

diagnosis.confirmed_mismatch: lib/letflow/dlq/entry.ex lines 98-127. The @doc above insert_changeset/2 (line 99-102) states 'status, retry_count, retry_history, tenant_id, and created_at are deliberately not castable here'. The actual cast/3 call (lines 107-125) lists all five as castable: :tenant_id, :status, :retry_count, :retry_history, :created_at all appear in the field list passed to cast/3. Confirmed by direct read of the file, not inferred from the issue text.
diagnosis.sole_caller_confirmed: grep for 'Entry.insert_changeset' and 'insert_changeset' across lib/ and test/ turns up exactly one call site: lib/letflow/dlq.ex:110, inside enqueue/2. (A separate, unrelated Entry.insert_changeset/2 exists on lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex:161 -- that is Letflow.ServiceCatalog.Entry, a different schema entirely; not in scope, not affected by this fix.) test/letflow/dlq_test.exs does not call Letflow.Dlq.Entry.insert_changeset/2 directly anywhere -- grep for 'insert_changeset' in that file returns nothing. So narrowing the cast list has exactly one call site to keep working (enqueue/2) and no direct-changeset test that would need updating for cast-list membership itself, though a new regression test per the issue's own candidate scope is still warranted.
diagnosis.enqueue2_sanitization_confirmed: lib/letflow/dlq.ex:81-113. enqueue/2 builds insert_attrs by Map.take/2 over attrs with an explicit allowlist of 12 keys (:entry_type, :instance_id, :reference_id, :reason, :full_reason, :error_detail, :error_chain, :source_payload, :context_json, :retry_limit, :first_failed_at, :last_failed_at -- notably NOT tenant_id/status/retry_count/retry_history/created_at), then Map.merge/2's in five trusted values: tenant_id (derived from opts[:prefix] via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, never from attrs), status: :pending, retry_count: 0, retry_history: [], created_at: DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.truncate(:second). This confirms the issue's description of the Map.take/Map.merge pattern verbatim.
diagnosis.created_at_is_not_ecto_autogenerated: Checked specifically per the task's instruction: Letflow.Dlq.Entry's schema block (entry.ex lines 43-67) declares created_at as a plain field(:created_at, :utc_datetime) with no default and no timestamps/1 macro (the moduledoc's own '## created_at, not timestamps/1' section, lines 31-36, explains this schema deliberately avoids timestamps/1 because the frontend contract names created_at specifically and has no updated_at at all). enqueue/2 sets created_at explicitly via DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.truncate(:second) at dlq.ex:106, merged into insert_attrs alongside tenant_id/status/retry_count/retry_history. So created_at IS genuinely caller-context-supplied at the enqueue/2 call boundary (not DB-generated, not autogenerate: true, not any Ecto timestamp mechanism) -- the issue's candidate scope is correct that it needs the same put_change/3 treatment as tenant_id, not a schema-default treatment like status/retry_count/retry_history.
diagnosis.schema_defaults_confirmed: status has default: :pending (entry.ex line 61), retry_count has default: 0 (line 55), retry_history has default: [] (line 54). tenant_id (line 44) and created_at (line 64) have no default. This matches the issue's claim exactly: the three fields with schema defaults are safe to drop from cast/3 entirely; the two without a default need an explicit write mechanism or validate_required/2 will fail once cast/3 no longer touches them.
diagnosis.precedent_pattern_confirmed: Read both cited precedents in full. lib/letflow/definitions/solution_pack_install.ex's insert_changeset/2 (lines 74-90): docstring claims status/uninstalled_at 'deliberately NOT castable', and cast/3's actual list (line 85: [:tenant_id, :pack_id, :installed_version, :installed_at]) genuinely excludes both -- they rely purely on the column default (:active). lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review.ex's insert_changeset/2 (lines 94-112): docstring claims status/approved_by/approved_at/superseded_by/row_version 'deliberately NOT castable', and cast/3's actual list (line 106: [:plan_digest, :def_type, :def_id, :serialised_plan, :requested_by]) genuinely excludes all five, relying on column defaults. Neither precedent needed a put_change/3 case because none of their protected fields lack a default -- Letflow.Dlq.Entry is a strictly harder case than either precedent because two of its five protected fields (tenant_id, created_at) have no default and are still required, genuine inputs at insert time. This is why the fix is not a straight copy of either precedent's shape.

task.root_cause: Stale docstring vs. stale code question, resolved: per source/discovered_in_run (WF02-REQ176-20260829, commit b5a028d), the docstring was written to describe the *intended* invariant (matching this codebase's two established precedents) but the cast/3 list was never actually narrowed to match it -- i.e., the implementation was left permissive, and the docstring was aspirational/incorrect from the same commit, not a later drift. No code change since has touched insert_changeset/2's cast list (single commit, no rework round touched this function per the design's own citation of commit 1959adf being the only rework, and that rework fixed a fabricated precedent citation in the design doc, unrelated to this function). SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged it as a non-blocking observation during REQ-176's own security gate (handoffs/WF02-REQ176-20260829/step-02c-security-reviewer.json's context.note, carried forward verbatim into step-02d's context.note for REVIEWER, and from there into this issue). task.candidate_scope_validation: The issue's own candidate_scope_for_whoever_picks_this_up holds up completely against the real source -- nothing it got wrong. Specifically confirmed correct: (1) :status, :retry_count, :retry_history should be dropped from cast/3 entirely, relying on their Ecto.Schema struct defaults (:pending/0/[]) -- verified these defaults exist and are correct at the schema level; (2) :tenant_id and :created_at should move from cast/3 membership to explicit put_change/3 calls reading those two keys out of attrs -- verified both are genuinely present as caller/enqueue-supplied keys in insert_attrs (not autogenerated, not schema-defaulted) so put_change/3 is the right mechanism, not e.g. a schema default or a timestamps/1 change; (3) the caller contract for enqueue/2 does not change -- it already builds and merges both keys into insert_attrs before calling insert_changeset/2, so put_change/3 reading them out of attrs inside insert_changeset/2 is a drop-in replacement for their prior cast/3 membership, no caller-side edit needed; (4) validate_required/2's existing list ([:tenant_id, :entry_type, :status, :retry_count, :created_at]) does not need to change -- put_change/3 sets the field's value in the changeset the same way cast/3 would have, so validate_required/2 still sees a present value for all five and continues to pass for real enqueue/2 calls.
task.one_addition_beyond_the_issues_own_scope: retry_history is NOT currently in the validate_required/2 list (only tenant_id/entry_type/status/retry_count/created_at are, entry.ex line 126) -- so dropping retry_history from cast/3 needs no validate_required/2 change either; this was implicit in the issue's text but worth stating explicitly so CODE-DESIGNER doesn't need to re-derive it: after the fix, cast/3's list becomes [:tenant_id, :entry_type, :instance_id, :reference_id, :reason, :full_reason, :error_detail, :error_chain, :source_payload, :context_json, :retry_limit, :first_failed_at, :last_failed_at] (tenant_id and created_at removed from this list, status/retry_count/retry_history also removed), and two put_change/3 calls are added reading :tenant_id and :created_at out of attrs, placed before validate_required/2 in the pipe chain so validate_required/2 sees the put_change'd values.
task.test_regression_recommendation_from_issu: Confirmed no existing test exercises insert_changeset/2 directly with unsanitized attrs (grep of test/letflow/dlq_test.exs found zero direct calls), so the issue's own recommendation -- add a changeset-level test asserting a raw/unfiltered attrs map with a caller-supplied tenant_id cannot override the put_change/3-set value -- is a genuinely new test, not a duplicate of existing coverage. result.summary: Diagnosis complete. Confirmed by direct source read (not from the issue report's prose): lib/letflow/dlq/entry.ex's insert_changeset/2 docstring (lines 99-102) claims status/retry_count/retry_history/tenant_id/created_at are 'deliberately not castable' but the actual cast/3 call (lines 107-125) casts all five. Sole caller is Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2 (lib/letflow/dlq.ex:81-113), which pre-sanitizes attrs via Map.take/2 (excluding all five protected fields) then Map.merge/2's in trusted values -- confirmed harmless today, exactly as the issue states. Grep confirms insert_changeset/2 has exactly one call site in the whole tree (dlq.ex:110); no test calls it directly, so narrowing the cast list breaks nothing existing. Root cause: the docstring was written aspirationally to match this codebase's two established precedents (lib/letflow/definitions/solution_pack_install.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review.ex, both read in full and confirmed to genuinely exclude their protected fields from cast/3) but the cast/3 list itself was never actually narrowed to match -- both docstring and permissive code date to the same original commit (b5a028d, REQ-176), not later drift. Key finding beyond the issue's own text: created_at is confirmed NOT Ecto-autogenerated -- it's a plain field(:created_at, :utc_datetime) with no default (the schema deliberately skips timestamps/1, per its own moduledoc), and enqueue/2 sets it explicitly via DateTime.utc_now(), so it genuinely needs the same put_change/3 treatment as tenant_id, not a schema-default treatment. The issue's candidate_scope_for_whoever_picks_this_up holds up completely against the real source with nothing wrong or incomplete -- validated every specific claim in it against the actual code. Step 0.5 registry lookup: no other resolved docs/issues/*.yaml entry matches this symptom, and no separate resolved duplicate exists for the former local id ISS-0353 (only ISS-0381.yaml's own note_on_id references it, documenting the id-rename, not a duplicate finding). This is a first-pass fix, not a recurrence. Routing to CODE-DESIGNER to design the insert_changeset/2 change (drop 5 fields from cast/3, add 2 put_change/3 calls for tenant_id/created_at, no caller-side change needed) plus the regression test TEST-DESIGNER should add afterward.
